name: Discovery Center at Deep Creek Lake State Park
address: Deep Creek Lake State Park, 898 State Park Road, Swanton, MD 21561
blurb: A 6,000 square foot nature center inside Deep Creek Lake State Park. Aquariums of fish out of the lake, an aviary of nine raptors that can't be released, a walk-through replica coal mine, and reptiles. It costs nothing to walk in, though you pay to get into the park.

hours.season: These are the summer hours. The sign on the door is headed "Welcome Summer", so treat them as seasonal until the winter ones are confirmed.
hours.note: DNR publishes no hours for this building anywhere online. These came off the door.

admission.note: Free. The park's own FAQ board says plainly: "The Discovery Center has no admission fee." You still pay to get into the park — $3 per person in-state and $5 out-of-state from Memorial Day to Labor Day, and $3 and $5 per vehicle the rest of the year.

website.label: Maryland DNR: Deep Creek Lake State Park

accessibility: DNR describes the restrooms as ADA accessible. Nothing published about the entrance or the exhibit floor.
parking: Its own parking lot at the building. The park's FAQ board gives directions to headquarters and to the beach as turns out of the Discovery Center parking lot, so it is also the landmark everything else here is described from.
inside: An aviary of nine non-releasable raptors: golden eagle, bald eagle, turkey vulture, peregrine falcon, red-tailed hawk and three species of owl
Aquariums of native fish and aquatic life out of the lake
Reptiles and amphibians, including eastern box turtles in an outdoor enclosure
A replica coal mine you walk through indoors
Exhibits on the hemlocks, the monarchs and how the forest filters the lake
A separate room given over to hands-on science
6,000 square feet in total, plus the Nature Shop
warnings: The center is free but the park gate is not. Budget the day-use fee on top.
Closed Monday and Tuesday in summer.

sources.label: Maryland DNR: Deep Creek Lake State Park
sources.note: The operator. Describes the Discovery Center, its size, the aviary of nine raptors, the aquariums, the replica coal mine, the ADA restrooms and the Nature Shop, and states that admission is free with donations encouraged. Gives 301-387-7067 for hours rather than publishing them.

The FAQ board inside states that the Discovery Center has no admission fee, gives the park's peak and off-season entry rates, and lists the camp office, Discovery Center and duty ranger numbers.

verifiedSource: Visited. Hours read off the door, admission and the rest off the park's own FAQ board
outstanding: Get the winter hours. The door sign is explicitly the summer one.

photos.alt: The main hall of a timber-framed nature center, with exposed beams, a pale wood floor, teal exhibit panels on hemlocks and forests, mounted fish and a turkey on the stone piers, and windows onto the trees.
photos.caption: The main hall. Bigger inside than it looks from the parking lot, and quiet on a Thursday morning.

photos.alt: An eastern box turtle with a yellow-patterned shell and orange head, on wood chips beside a shallow purple water dish.
photos.caption: One of the box turtles, out by its water dish. The reptiles are the easiest thing here to actually see.

reports.what: Open Wednesday to Sunday, 10am to 4pm on the summer sign. No admission fee, per the park's FAQ board. There's a parking lot at the building. Photographed the door sign and the board.

name: Garrett County History Museum
blurb: The county historical society's main museum, in downtown Oakland. Two hundred years of Garrett County in one building: the B&O Railroad, the Oakland and Deer Park hotels, the schools, the opera house, the coal mines.

hours.note: The society doesn't say whether these hours hold through the winter.

admission.note: Not confirmed. The society publishes no admission price and no donation policy on its own site.

inside: Artifacts across roughly two hundred years of county history
The B&O Railroad in Garrett County
The Oakland and Deer Park hotels
County schools and the opera house
Coal mining
warnings: Closed Sunday through Tuesday. Four days a week is easy to get wrong on a weekend trip.

name: Garrett County Museum of Transportation
blurb: Two floors of how people and things moved around this county: carriages, sleighs, automobiles, boats, fire equipment. The upstairs gallery is given over to the history of Deep Creek Lake itself. Open for the warm half of the year only.

hours.season: 6 May 2026 through the Autumn Glory Festival. Shut for the winter.
hours.note: Autumn Glory is the second full weekend in October, so the season ends around then.

admission.note: Not confirmed. The society publishes no admission price and no donation policy on its own site.

inside: Carriages, sleighs and buggies
Automobiles and boats
Fire department equipment
The Deep Creek Gallery upstairs: the history of the lake and the state parks around it
Rotating exhibits
warnings: Shut all winter. The 2026 season runs 6 May to Autumn Glory, so a January trip is wasted.
Closed Sunday through Tuesday even in season.

name: Oakland B&O Museum
blurb: The 1884 B&O depot in the middle of Oakland, restored and run as a railroad museum. Model trains, telegraph equipment and station fittings inside; a Baldwin steam locomotive and a caboose parked outside. Open every day, which almost nothing else here is.

hours.note: The museum is volunteer-staffed, so the published hours depend on someone turning up. Call ahead if the trip is long.

admission.note: Not confirmed. The museum publishes no admission price on its own site.

inside: The restored 1884 depot, by the Baltimore architects Baldwin & Pennington
Model trains
Telegraph equipment and station artifacts
A gift shop of train-themed things
Outside: the 1920 Baldwin locomotive 476, B&O caboose C-2884, and interpretive plaques
warnings: Volunteer-run. "Open every day" is the intention, not a guarantee.

sources.label: Oakland, Maryland B&O Museum: visit us
sources.note: The operator. Gives "Open Every Day, 10 am to 3 pm", the East Liberty Street address, the gift shop, the volunteer-led tours, and the indoor and outdoor exhibits. Publishes no admission price and no phone number.

sources.label: Oakland B&O Museum: the 1920 Baldwin Steam Locomotive plaque
sources.note: Interpretive plaque on the plaza, photographed 5 August 2026. Gives the engine's full history: built 1920 by Baldwin as number 40 for the Jonesboro, Lake City and Eastern Railroad, renumbered 76 in 1925, sold to the Mississippian Railway in 1947, then to a Pennsylvania scenic railway in 1967 and the Gettysburg line, then to the Steam Railroading Institute in 2005. Bought by the museum in 2017 with a donation from the Daniel E. Offutt III Charitable Trust, moved to Oakland in July 2018 and restored for display by Diversified Rail Services. Renumbered 476 because it resembles the B&O E-39 class.

outstanding: Get a phone number. Their own site doesn't publish one.
Ask what it costs to get in.
Ask whether the every-day hours hold through the winter.
Ask about restrooms and step-free access into an 1884 depot.

photos.alt: A black steam locomotive numbered 476 with white-rimmed driving wheels, standing on brick paving beside the museum with a red caboose behind it and storm cloud overhead.
photos.caption: Engine 476 outside the 1884 depot. It's on brick in the open, so you can walk round it whether the museum is open or not.

photos.alt: The same locomotive side-on, showing the cab, boiler and running gear, with a viewing platform and steps alongside.
photos.caption: Side on. There are steps up to a platform so you can look into the cab.

photos.alt: A bright red Baltimore and Ohio caboose lettered B&O C-2884, with white window frames and a yellow handrail, on brick paving.
photos.caption: Caboose C-2884, coupled up behind the engine.

photos.alt: An interpretive plaque headed 1920 Baldwin Steam Locomotive, with several paragraphs of text and a black and white photograph of the engine in service on the Mississippian Railway.
photos.caption: The plaque tells you the engine never actually ran for the B&O — the museum adopted it and renumbered it.

photos.alt: A wider view of the museum plaza with the locomotive, the caboose and the depot buildings under heavy cloud.
photos.caption: The whole display from the far end of the plaza.

photos.alt: A white and yellow Victorian gazebo with a shingled roof and turned balusters, on a brick apron beside a yellow clapboard building with a tall MUSEUM sign and a cupola.
photos.caption: The gazebo on the lawn beside the museum. The vertical MUSEUM sign is how you find the place from the street.

onSite.label: Outside, always
onSite.note: The locomotive, the caboose and the plaques stand on open brick paving in the middle of town. You can walk round them when the museum itself is shut, which matters given it is volunteer-staffed.

onSite.label: Engine 476
onSite.note: A 1920 Baldwin. It was built as number 40 for a railroad in Arkansas, ran most of its life as 76, and never worked for the B&O at all. The museum bought it in 2018 and renumbered it 476 because it closely matches the B&O's own E-39 class.

onSite.label: The gazebo
onSite.note: A Victorian gazebo on the lawn beside the museum, on brick paving. Somewhere to sit that isn't the plaza, and it's out in the open like the trains.

reports.what: The locomotive and caboose are on open brick paving outside the depot, walk-round any time. Photographed the engine, the caboose and the interpretive plaque.

name: Ruth Enlow Library of Garrett County
operator: Ruth Enlow Library of Garrett County
blurb: The county library, five branches, free to walk into. On a wet afternoon it's the most reliable indoor room in Garrett County: warm, quiet, has a bathroom, and nobody minds how long you sit there. Every branch keeps different hours, and three of the five shut at lunchtime on Saturday.

hours.note: These are the Oakland hours. The other four branches all differ — see the branch table.
